Asian shares rose on Nov 18 after Nvidia posted a better-than-expected sales forecast, snapping four consecutive days of regional losses. MSCI's broadest Asia-Pacific index outside Japan advanced 0.9%, led by South Korea's KOSPI gaining as much as 3.3%. Japan's Nikkei 225 climbed 0.6%, while US S&P 500 e-mini futures were up 0.5%.

Nvidia shares rose 4.7% in after-hours trading, reporting quarterly revenue above forecasts in its first earnings report since Jensen Huang's abrupt departure as CEO in November. The gains came despite the Wall Street Journal reporting that the SEC is probing Nvidia over recent turmoil.

Jake Behan, head of capital markets at Direxion in New York, said: "I've looked at this whole week as a referendum on AI." He added that Anthropic was about to give investors a read on appetite for the next generation of AI companies. Overnight, Wall Street stocks sold off again with the S&P 500 down 1% before Nvidia's report.

Oil prices edged lower, with Brent crude futures 0.2% below US$93 a barrel as Asian trading began. The benchmark rebounded from Nov 17 declines amid worries about continuing tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and expectations of falling US crude inventories against projected supply surplus from recovering Middle East exports.

Westpac analysts noted: "Risk sentiment remained firmly on the defensive overnight, with the tech-led sell-off extending across global markets." The next major AI industry health check would come as Anthropic prepared to price its shares later Nov 18 ahead of a market debut that could value the company at up to US$1.4 trillion (S$1.8 trillion), per Bloomberg News.

The yen was 0.1% weaker against the dollar at 159.49, while Japan's exports rose for a 14th successive month in October on semiconductor-related demand. The US dollar index climbed 0.1% to 103.66, reaching its highest level since April 2, 2025 — the date of Trump's Liberation Day tariff announcement.

The yield on the US 10-year Treasury rose 2.2 basis points to 5.123%. On Nov 17, St. Louis Fed president Alberto Musalem said the Federal Reserve may need several rate hikes to control inflation and should act soon. In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin was up 0.9% at US$64,862.82 while ether rose 1.0% at US$1,823.74.
items.title: Asia stocks rebound on Nvidia beat as Anthropic IPO looms

On Nov 17, Nvidia reported fourth-quarter revenue guidance of US$130 billion plus or minus 3%, above Wall Street's average estimate of US$125.25 billion per LSEG data, while adjusted gross margin is expected at 71% to 72% versus an analyst estimate of 71.7%. The outlook assumes no data-center chip sales to China. Shares rose nearly 4% in extended trading but remained down about 17% for the year through the Nov 17 close, with the company valued at roughly US$3.8 trillion (S$4.9 trillion). Interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress said 'our momentum is real,' without addressing leadership uncertainty, noting that Vera Rubin was off to an explosive start and the roadmap remained on track.

The results provided some relief after longtime leader Jensen Huang's resignation plunged the chipmaker into crisis. Huang exited three decades of founder-led control over Nvidia's chip roadmap, customer deals, and Washington ties, making execution a bigger risk than near-term AI demand, analysts say. The board is not considering his return despite a growing 'Stand With Jensen' campaign; instead it created a committee on national security and export controls as its first major governance move since his departure.

Huang resigned after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang and two Nvidia employees. US intelligence agencies are trying to determine the extent of Alice Huang's ties to China's Ministry of State Security and what information she may have passed to Beijing. Washington has tightened licensing rules for chip shipments to South-east Asia and overseas data centers serving Chinese firms, while lawmakers prepare to question Huang.

Investors remain uneasy about AI spending after Democrats' midterm sweep fueled fears of tougher scrutiny and slower data-center expansion. They also want to know whether Nvidia's next CEO will continue financing customers, a practice critics call circular. The Nov 17 results offered a first read on Vera Rubin, Nvidia's newest generation of AI processors and successor to Grace Blackwell; the company said in August that Vera Rubin would account for about a fifth of data-center revenue in the October quarter and forecast 70% revenue growth in the next fiscal year.

Nvidia's third-quarter revenue more than doubled to US$115.84 billion, beating analysts' estimate of $109.11 billion per Reuters. The company has topped Wall Street's revenue expectations for 17 straight quarters, and adjusted gross margin rose to 74.9% from 73.5% a year earlier, also beating the analyst estimate of 74.1%, despite soaring memory prices and production ramps.
items.title: Nvidia posts strong Q3 results amid post-Huang leadership uncertainty and national security scrutiny

items.summary: Nvidia reported on Tuesday that its equity stake in private companies is now worth $65.5 billion, up from the $22 billion it had reported in January. The increase reflects both new investments and significant markups of existing portfolio companies. Over the past quarter alone, Nvidia invested $16 billion into equities, while spending $58 billion over the past nine months of its fiscal year; this compares to just $5 billion for the same period a year earlier, in November 2025. The company stated that it invests with the goal of expanding the AI ecosystem by backing startups it considers “game changers and market makers.” Over nearly three years since announcing this strategy in late 2023, Nvidia has invested in nearly 350 startups according to PitchBook, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Thinking Machines, Reflection, Lambda, Nscale, and Crusoe. Beyond startup equity, Nvidia has become a major financier of data center construction, reporting $118 billion in guarantees with $105 billion backing the backstop for OpenAI's $500 billion data center in Ohio. During Tuesday's earnings call, Kress said Nvidia would continue providing financing assistance to strong customers but added that “as the market matures and additional sources of capital become available,” the company would be “rigorously evaluating future investments, commitments, and guarantees.” She also stated that the company intends to return all excess free cash flow net of strategic uses to shareholders during this quarter and going forward. Investors have told TechCrunch that Huang's dealmaking has been a source of concern for Kress, who is expected to take a more conservative approach under her interim leadership as Jensen Huang transitions out.
items.title: Nvidia's startup stakes ballooned to $65B, but Huang's exit puts future deals in doubt

items.summary: During Nvidia's Tuesday earnings call—the first since CEO Jensen Huang resigned—interim CEO Colette Kress reaffirmed the company's commitment to open source AI. In her opening remarks, Kress stated that Nvidia remains committed to fostering a vibrant open model ecosystem so every country, company, and industry can build its own intelligence. She noted that open models are accelerating AI adoption, citing a 35-fold year-over-year surge in weekly token volume on OpenRouter, including a 3.5-fold increase over the past three months. Kress also addressed Nvidia's plans for Hugging Face, which the company agreed to acquire for $12.9 billion in September and would make the second-largest acquisition in Nvidia's history. The platform serves more than 18 million developers and 200,000 companies, and remains on track to join Nvidia despite Huang's departure. Kress said that together they will scale its platform and make intelligence more open, capable, and accessible. Huang had heavily advocated for open source AI technology; his ouster prompted Hugging Face's CEO to call it a sad day while promising to keep fighting for open-source AI harder than ever. So far, Nvidia's plans for Hugging Face appear unchanged, though the acquisition was not directly addressed during the Q&A portion of the earnings call. Huang resigned from his position as CEO following news about his extramarital affairs, including one with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed who is suspected of being a Chinese spy. He has also been accused of having extramarital affairs with two direct reports and is set to testify before Congress by Thanksgiving. The SEC is investigating Nvidia over whether the company's disclosures misled investors, per WSJ reporting. Within Nvidia, Huang had pushed for development of the Nemotron family of open-weight AI models built for long-running agentic AI systems and reasoning workloads. On the call, Kress noted that Nemotron is now the most widely used U.S. open model on OpenRouter, where developers start to build their own intelligence, describing this foundation as empowering the ecosystem.
items.title: Nvidia reaffirms open source AI commitment after Jensen Huang's exit

items.summary: The Compute Platform team at Databricks provisions virtual machines and coordinates cluster creation across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud for classic compute workloads. Historically they protected the system with fixed API request-rate limits—accepting a set number of requests per time window—which worked when available capacity and per-request work were predictable but became hard to tune as workload mix and dependency failures grew. Conservative limits rejected customer requests even during spare capacity, yet still accepted them while dependencies slowed; engineers manually lowered and raised the limits around incidents. The team replaced this with adaptive concurrency control: a slot-based limit on active cluster-creation workflows that expands when capacity is available and contracts under congestion signals like provisioning latency or thread-pool saturation, keeping a fixed API request-rate ceiling as a final guardrail against exceptionally high incoming traffic. They explain the difference using a kitchen analogy—a fixed rule of ten new orders per minute turns away work despite spare cooks and keeps accepting it faster than an oven can finish meals, whereas tracking in-progress meals with adjustable slots lets fewer start when capacity falls and more begin as it recovers. A single API call only validates and records a request before returning; the actual provisioning—validating dependencies, updating state, and launching VMs—runs asynchronously for minutes while the handler completes in milliseconds, so one request can provision many VMs and its duration depends on dependency health. During shared slowdowns more workflows take longer simultaneously, leaving far more work in flight at the same incoming rate; when a dependency degrades, retries from accepted work pile onto it, causing further failures and yet more retries—a retry storm that persists after traffic normalizes because request-rate limits do not see internal retries. A lower fixed rate only buys headroom by rejecting healthy-period work, while raising it uses capacity better but accepts more during degradation; one number cannot cover both days. The team distinguishes two failure situations behind a 'too many requests' message: shared-dependency slowdowns where the customer's traffic is normal and asking them to change behavior misattributes a service problem, versus an unusually large burst from one tenant competing for resources while the service stays healthy—so they track system health, per-tenant demand, and scheduling decisions separately. For long-running operations that take minutes, queuing accepted requests with bounded wait times lets bursts drain rather than returning immediate errors followed by retries, provided waiting fits each request's deadline; an unbounded queue can turn a brief disruption into hours of delay, so they bound backlog size and expiration time, keep queued records small instead of running workers holding scarce resources, and plan for the worst-case backlog to discard cheaply. A scheduler also decides which work goes first under contention—balancing tenant shares with letting tenants use idle capacity while preserving fair access—and this choice shapes whether many customers each see one slow request or one customer sees many; a successful API response does not guarantee immediate launch or completion within fixed time. The initial rollout analysis reported 7.5× higher default cluster-creation request-rate limits, more than 99.99% fewer cluster-creation rate-limit errors in the reported scope, and removal of over a hundred customer-specific rate-limit overrides in scope; since then few customers have hit the higher limits and no new manual overrides were added for those limits. They note open design questions—weighted slots or separate limits when operations carry very different resource costs, where to apply control so one slow dependency does not hold up unrelated work—and that pairing concurrency limits with retry backoff and attempt caps reduces pressure during cloud-provider recovery; the controller counts active provisioning workflows only, not running clusters or allocated VMs and vCPUs. They also point readers to High Performance Ratelimiting at Databricks for enforcing API quotas at scale as a complementary problem.
items.title: How Databricks Raised Cluster Creation Rate Limits by 7.5× Using Adaptive Concurrency Control

items.summary: At the Microsoft Ignite 2026 keynote, Satya Nadella introduced two new frontier AI models built for 'everyday' coding tasks. The lead model, MAI Code 2, is claimed to deliver 96% of Claude Opus 5.5 performance at 5% of its price. A companion model, MAI Code 2 Flash, is described as comparable to the lower-end GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5, also at considerably lower cost. Microsoft states that both models offer performance similar to GPT-6.1 Sol or Opus 5.5 while costing a fraction of those offerings. The article notes these are usage-based metrics based on API usage; paying subscribers will not automatically receive equivalent results for five dollars, and the figures reflect introductory pricing with a reported 50% discount rather than $0.0005 per request. Alongside Code 2 and Code 2 Flash, Microsoft announced MAI Work Flash, derived from Code 2 Flash, which can generate Excel formulas, work with Word documents and instructions, track decisions, and extract information from Teams. The article explains that coding agents serve as effective training grounds for non-coding 'work' agents because code output is highly measurable; agentic productivity tools like ChatGPT Work and Claude Cowork originated as coding harnesses such as Claude Code and OpenAI Codex before being repackaged for non-programmers. Microsoft has a multi-billion-dollar investment in OpenAI dating back to 2023, but the new home-grown models could reduce reliance on external providers like Anthropic and OpenAI by handling high volumes of basic, routine AI requests across Copilot, Microsoft 365, and Fabric as optional choices. Nadella emphasized how central AI has become in Microsoft's operations, with most prior AI work involving token fees paid to frontier model providers or customers doing the same. The article runs hypothetical numbers: a company spending $0.01 per request could drop that cost to $0.001 per request; a daily inference cost of $100,000 (a figure likened to Microsoft) could fall to about $100,000 annually reduced—dropping from the original million-dollar daily cost—and total roughly $325 million saved over a year. The article notes there is no direct evidence that Microsoft intends to replace frontier providers' offerings, though it frames this as an interesting story of vertical integration and control for its own software economy. On limitations, the author flags potential benchmark cherry-picking while expressing doubt that Microsoft is padding numbers since it benefits more than even its customers; Microsoft also stated these models are not designed for the most challenging agentic or research workloads—suitable for tasks like reformatting PowerPoint but unlikely to solve decades-old mathematics problems. The article highlights that the new models performed unusually well on visualization assignments, a good fit for UI design and slide production.
items.title: Microsoft Unveils MAI Code Models at Ignite 2026; Claims Near-Opus Performance at a Fraction of Cost and Reduced Provider Dependence

items.summary: Google is replacing its Gemini feature 'Gems' with a new capability called 'Skills,' effective November 17, 2026. While the Gems interface itself is being retired, any existing Gems will not be lost; they automatically convert to Skills, though users may transfer them manually if they wish to begin using them immediately. Accessing the now-retiring Gems section requires going through Settings, where a message informs users that 'Starting November 17, 2026, we'll automatically begin migrating all of your Gems to Skills.' The cutoff date for accessing existing Gems is December 16, 2026; Workspace business, enterprise, and non-profit accounts will instead be cut off in March 2027, while Workspace education accounts are scheduled for a June 2027 cutoff. Functionally, a Gemini Skill operates much like a Gem: users describe the specific situations when Gemini should apply it automatically and specify what they want it to do, ideally with concrete examples of desired output. Google's own example involves a marketing team sharing a brand-voice skill that references their brand guidelines document in Drive, or a team lead sharing an onboarding skill based on the team handbook. The principal distinction is structural: whereas Gems were standalone chats, Skills are custom instructions that function within any conversation. Users may create as many Skills as they like, but only 100 can be active at once. Google has carried over two features from Gems to ease adoption of Skills. First, users can share a Skill with other people and choose whether the recipient may edit it or view it only; sharing is done via the three-bar menu in the top left > Customize > Skills, where permissions can also be viewed or changed. A caveat noted is that at present Skills can only be shared through the Gemini web app, not the mobile app. Second, when creating a Skill, users may include files up to 100MB from other Google products such as Drive, Photos, and Notebook, along with local device files; these are referenced every time the Skill runs and update in real time per Google's description. These file-sharing capabilities previously existed within Gems and are being moved into Skills so that the new feature is more comparable to its predecessor.
items.title: Google Retires Gemini Gems and Migrates to Skills Starting November 17, 2026

items.summary: Prime Minister Lawrence Wong announced his upcoming visit to China this week, first attending the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen and then visiting Beijing. He framed the trip around a shared appreciation of openness and engagement as an important foundation of Singapore-China relations, arguing that keeping countries' doors open is more important than ever amid growing global uncertainty and fragmentation. Wong highlighted Shenzhen's transformation from a small town into a global technology hub over just a few decades as evidence of China's reform and opening up, drawing a parallel to how openness shaped Singapore's own development despite its limited resources. He noted that the two countries' friendship predates diplomatic relations established in 1990, with earlier leaders including Mr Lee Kuan Yew and Mr Deng Xiaoping laying foundational ties built on mutual respect, trust and understanding; last year they commemorated 35 years of diplomatic relations. Wong described three government-to-government projects that illustrate the evolving partnership: the Suzhou Industrial Park to support industrial development, the Tianjin Eco-City to explore sustainable urban living, and more recently the Chongqing Connectivity Initiative focused on strengthening trade between western China and South-east Asia. He emphasized that each project reflected its time's opportunities and priorities, showing how cooperation has continually adapted with both sides learning from one another. Wong also noted that since their bilateral Free Trade Agreement came into force in 2009, it has been progressively upgraded to keep pace with changing needs, extending beyond traditional trade and investment into the digital economy, sustainability and innovation. Looking ahead, he pointed to China's 15th Five-Year Plan emphasizing high-quality development, innovation and improving people's livelihoods, alongside Singapore's completed Economic Strategy Review aimed at strengthening competitiveness through new technologies and good jobs; both face common challenges including rapid technological change, ageing populations, workforce skills needs, and the transition toward greener growth. Wong argued these shared challenges present opportunities for cooperation, particularly in applying artificial intelligence across industries and developing emerging technologies. He stressed that Singapore remains a firm supporter of an open, inclusive and rules-based economic architecture, believing regional cooperation should bring countries closer rather than divide them into competing blocs, even as he acknowledged governments' understandable responsibility to safeguard their economies against disruptions from rising geopolitical tensions and trade barriers. Wong noted Singapore's upcoming ASEAN chairmanship next year will focus on deepening regional integration and expanding cooperation with all partners including China, building on the ASEAN-China Free Trade Area whose latest upgrade covers digital and green economies, supply chain connectivity and innovation. He praised China's APEC theme of "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together" as timely given its focus on openness, innovation and cooperation, expressing Singapore's commitment to working with all APEC economies in Shenzhen and building on those efforts when Singapore chairs APEC in 2030. Wong concluded by reaffirming the All-Round High-Quality Future-Oriented Partnership between the two countries as reflecting both the breadth of their cooperation and a shared commitment to take it further, arguing that at a time of growing global divisions, strengthening connections rather than erecting barriers can help build a more resilient and prosperous Asia-Pacific. Wong's remarks were delivered in his capacity as Singapore's Prime Minister during an official visit tied to APEC participation; the article presents these views without independent verification or additional analysis beyond what he stated.
items.title: Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong on Strengthening Singapore-China Relations Ahead of APEC Visit

items.summary:
Historically, resolving customer records to a person-based ID such as RampID required exporting PII to an outside service, waiting for a match file, and loading it back in. Each step added a pipeline to maintain, a copy of sensitive data to govern, and a delay before results were usable. Packaged clean rooms on Databricks remove that round-trip by bringing the identity service into the customer's own environment.

LiveRamp Embedded Identity delivers this through LiveRamp's packaged clean room mode. A packaged clean room is one in which a provider supplies an analysis and a customer runs it against its own data without seeing the code, with neither party able to see the other's data assets. The computation happens on serverless compute in a Databricks-managed central clean room that no party administers. LiveRamp provides the identity graph and resolution code; the customer supplies PII touchpoints and receives RampIDs.

This differs from a standard, approval-based Databricks clean room, where every collaborator is a peer: anyone can add data or notebooks, approvers read notebook source, and each notebook needs approval before it runs. In a packaged clean room only the provider adds code; the customer sees notebook and JAR names but not their contents, there is no approval step because the customer cannot review the code, and the customer alone triggers runs while receiving output.

The architecture relies on three components. The central clean room is Databricks-managed and separate from both workspaces. OpenSharing (formerly Delta Sharing) is the open sharing protocol built into Clean Rooms; neither party copies tables in—instead each adds Unity Catalog assets, and OpenSharing grants the central clean room read-only access to them live, without replication, so each run reads the current version of the customer's input table rather than an extract from last week. The connection uses Databricks-to-Databricks sharing, keeping Unity Catalog governance on both sides: the provider controls which assets it exposes, the customer controls which tables it adds, and sharing activity is audited for both. OpenSharing also carries models, unstructured data, JAR files, private libraries, python wheels, and more.

A single run writes to two schemas delivered via the same OpenSharing mechanism into catalogs specified at set-up, found in Catalog Explorer's Shares received section; these can be queried immediately but must be copied down into a customer's own cloud storage for long-term (beyond 30 days) use. Both parties see every run's history—status, timing, and notebook—and both receive the shared output schema where LiveRamp writes metrics and logs. Because the customer owns data and LiveRamp owns code, neither has the full picture alone when a run fails; the shared view lets both teams troubleshoot without exposing data.

For identity resolution specifically, the split protects both sides: LiveRamp's matching logic stays its intellectual property and invisible to the customer, while the customer's PII and resolved results stay private. To run it, a user needs a LiveRamp agreement with Identity API credentials, a Unity Catalog workspace, and the CREATE CLEAN ROOM privilege; they prepare an input table of PII touchpoints and a metadata table holding LiveRamp credentials and run settings, then create the clean room from the LiveRamp tile under Identity Resolution Providers. If storage sits behind a firewall or private endpoint, SecureConnect must be enabled first.

Billing falls to the creator of the clean room at Jobs Serverless rates, starting only for each run with no idle environment to maintain. Output tables are retained for 30 days. The result is a RampID table in the customer's own Unity Catalog ready for customer 360, audience building, activation, partner collaboration, and measurement—no exports to schedule, no match files to wait on, and no extra copies of PII to govern.
items.title: Packaged Clean Rooms for RampID Identity Resolution on Databricks

items.summary: Electric power tool brand Greenworks is expanding its battery-forward lineup by launching OPTIMUS, an all-new go-anywhere electric side-by-side utility vehicle (SxS). First shown at Equip Exposition 2026 in Kentucky last month, the redesigned UTV is described as the biggest and newest addition to the company's commercial ecosystem. Greenworks claims it integrates its purpose-built equipment and power platforms for professional property maintenance customers. Yin Chen, CEO of Greenworks, says OPTIMUS extends the brand's vision of pushing battery power beyond industry expectations, covering everything from maintained-property equipment to utility vehicles and charging systems. The vehicle is built around a 400V high-voltage electrical platform that mates two compact electric motors combining for 110 equivalent hp. Those motors draw on a 19 kWh lithium-ion battery pack with enough efficiency to reach a 40 MPH top speed and cover up to 68 miles of range under typical operating conditions. For hauling, OPTIMUS offers buyers a 2,500 lb towing capacity and 1,300 lb payload capacity along with 11 full inches of ground clearance and a 6,000 lb electric winch. Independent suspension, oversized all-terrain tires, torque vectoring differentials, and multiple terrain modes round out the spec sheet for demanding off-road applications. The article also references related items: Club Car Urban as an electric pickup in US; John Deere's updated Gator GX and GX Crew electric UTVs for 2026; CFMoto U6 electric side-by-side UTV; plus a promotional EnergySage solar installer service offering savings of 20-30% compared to going it alone. The article notes the '100 equivalent' hp figure is marked with an uncertainty indicator, and that Greenworks uses '?' notation around some specs in its own text.
items.title: Greenworks launches OPTIMUS electric UTV with over 100 equivalent hp and 68-mile range

items.summary: America's largest weapons manufacturers face a January 1 Pentagon deadline requiring them to prove their magnets are free of Chinese rare earths, even though dysprosium and terbium—the two heavy rare earths used to keep powerful magnets working under extreme temperatures in fighter aircraft, missiles, and other advanced military equipment—are nearly entirely controlled by Beijing. China controls close to 100% of the processing for these metals. To address this dependency, Washington has proposed making 200 acres of a 43,000-acre Army depot in Utah available for REalloys (NASDAQ: ALOY) to build a heavy rare earth processing plant under a lease that could last up to 75 years. On November 3, REalloys and the U.S. Army signed a non-binding term sheet at Tooele Army Depot; REalloys would finance, construct, and operate the facility while the Army retains first opportunity to purchase its dysprosium and terbium production. The timing aligns with China's pause on expanded rare earth export controls, which Beijing extended two months to January 10, 2027—nine days after the Pentagon ban takes effect. Defense contractors have requested more time but Washington has kept the deadline in place. REalloys holds an advantage through its developing North American supply chain that converts rare earth oxides into metals; it is working with the Saskatchewan Research Council on what they describe as North America's first fully integrated commercial rare earth processing and metallization operation, while retired four-star General Jack Keane, a board member, warned China has made clear it is prepared to use this dependence as leverage. The Army lease would give REalloys long-term industrial presence on an American military installation with the Pentagon seeking first access; Waksman told Fox Business that the structure lets the Army expand the critical minerals industrial base without putting taxpayer dollars at risk, and CEO Lipi Sternheim said it puts part of the rare earth supply chain under military oversight. Keane called the term sheet 'an important step toward bringing heavy rare earth processing onto a U.S. defense installation.' The arrangement still requires REalloys and the Army to complete environmental review, permitting, and requirements before signing the final lease; the term sheet provides for a 50-year lease with a 25-year extension option, with REalloys paying fair-market rent plus participation rent once commercial operations begin. On processing capacity, magnet makers buy dysprosium and terbium as metal rather than oxide, and China ran nearly 100% of global heavy rare earth metallization until recently; outside China only a handful of plants make these metals—Less Common Metals in the U.K., the Korean Metals Plant at Ochang (which has made initial sales), and REalloys' Euclid, Ohio operation as the only North American heavy rare earth metallization capability. REalloys is scaling its $40 million plant built at SRC in Saskatoon before moving to Ohio; it will produce about 30 tonnes of dysprosium metal and 15 tonnes of terbium metal a year, with a provisional patent on a hydrofluoric acid-free fluorination process that could reduce capex, opex, and improve sustainability. Chairman Stephen duMont called the plant 'a critical link that's never existed at scale in the West,' while REalloys told Oilprice.com that dysprosium and terbium metals represent a major bottleneck for advanced magnet manufacturing. Within its integrated supply chain, SRC's CEO calls the partnership 'the Western hemisphere's first end-to-end rare earth metal capability.' REalloys' Euclid subsidiary Terves is developing engineering design for a 300-ton-a-year samarium and gadolinium metal plant under a Defense Logistics Agency contract awarded in March. REalloys holds rights to about 80% of SRC's expanded output—525 tonnes of NdPr metal, 30 tonnes of dysprosium oxide, and 15 tonnes of terbium oxide a year—and targets first NdPr metal from SRC in Q1 2027 with the dysprosium and terbium metallization plant commissioning in Q1 2028. On feedstock, REalloys locked in a 15-year offtake for 15% of Phase 1 production from Critical Metals' Tanbreez project in Greenland; it also signed non-binding agreements in Montana and Wyoming plus an Appalachian material memorandum of understanding. The company raised about $100 million in June and held $122.4 million in cash at quarter-end, saying its cash covers the Saskatchewan and heavy metallization projects through commissioning. Critical Metals Corp. (NASDAQ: CRML), which closed its merger with European Lithium on November 5 to own all of Greenland's Tanbreez project up from 42% at year start, reported about $264.5 million in cash after the merger and plans a definitive feasibility study by Q4 2027; first ore is not expected until late 2028 to early 2029, so Tanbreez feedstock remains a story for after the January deadline. Elsewhere, MP Materials (NYSE: MP) said on November 5 it completed General Motors' magnet qualification at its Independence plant in Fort Worth, Texas, with saleable deliveries and revenue starting Q4; that segment brought $18.6 million last quarter against $147.7 million total revenue, down 15% from a year earlier partly due to the start-up of magnet production there. In Oklahoma, USA Rare Earth (NASDAQ: USAR) made its first commercial magnet sale in September shipping sintered block magnets from Stillwater; Q3 revenue was only $3.0 million though it ended September with about $1.2 billion in cash and restricted cash after closing on Serra Verde with shipments beginning October and first sales recorded November. Further out, NioCorp Developments (NASDAQ: NB) is building the Elk Creek mine in southeast Nebraska to produce dysprosium oxide and terbium oxide alongside niobium and scandium; The U.S. Export-Import Bank said in October it still targets debt covering about 65% of roughly $1.85 billion in upfront costs subject to due diligence, and NioCorp signed a non-binding memorandum with Lockheed Martin for up to 15 tonnes a year of scandium oxide. Lockheed, RTX, General Dynamics, and Northrop now must hand the Pentagon a paper trail for every magnet installed—almost every dysprosium and terbium trail leading to China—with the White House order requiring them to trace 'all components, parts, equipment, software, and materials' back to raw-material origins; REalloys is building a trail that never touches China via Greenland feedstock from Tanbreez, separated oxide from Saskatchewan, metal from Euclid, and 200 acres on an Army base in Utah. This publication contains forward-looking statements involving risks and uncertainties that may cause actual results to differ due to changing governmental laws and policies among other factors; neither the author nor Oilprice.com was paid for this communication concerning REalloys (NASDAQ: ALOY), though its owner holds shares or options of the featured company, creating a stated conflict requiring independent due diligence.
items.title: Pentagon Deadline Drives REalloys Rare Earth Magnet Push in Utah

items.summary: SolarEdge Technologies has unveiled its new Duo Power Optimizer, a U.S.-manufactured solution aimed at simplifying commercial and industrial (C&I) solar installations without sacrificing system performance. Announced November 16 ahead of RE+ 2026 in Las Vegas, the product introduces a 2:1 architecture that allows one optimizer to connect two solar modules, cutting the number of power optimizers by 50% compared with traditional one-to-one designs while retaining independent maximum power point tracking (MPPT) for each module. For developers, EPCs and installers managing large-scale rooftop and distributed generation projects, this reduction targets fewer components to purchase, wire and install, along with streamlined balance-of-system requirements and reduced installation labor. The Duo addresses the limitation of conventional string inverter systems, where an underperforming module can affect the output of an entire string; by allowing each module to operate independently, it limits the impact of shading, degradation or performance differences between panels. Each optimizer features two input pairs: a shorter connection for the nearest module and a pre-extended connection for the adjacent module, reducing excess wiring and eliminating field-made jumpers. The configuration also accommodates modules with different orientations, making it relevant for east-west and dual-tilt racking applications. On safety, SolarEdge extends its Sense Connect technology to the optimizer's input and output connectors to monitor connector temperatures and identify developing issues before they escalate into overheating or electrical arcs. It introduces an industry-first approach to arc fault detection in which every optimizer acts as an individual arc sensor rather than relying exclusively on detection at the inverter, distributing monitoring throughout the array so faults can be identified closer to their source. SolarEdge says this provides coverage across strings with up to 3,280 feet of total cable length between the inverter and optimizer, potentially improving troubleshooting and maintenance efficiency. Manufactured at SolarEdge's Florida facility, the Duo is designed to meet U.S. Domestic Content and Foreign Entity of Concern (FEOC) requirements; its domestic-content eligibility levels are consistent with those of previous U.S.-manufactured power optimizers, subject to applicable tax guidance and project-specific requirements. For SolarEdge, the product combines installation efficiency, system-level safety, and domestic manufacturing into a single effort that does not fundamentally change the value proposition of module-level optimization but instead makes it more economical and easier to deploy at scale. The company will showcase the Duo Power Optimizer at RE+ 2026 in Las Vegas.
items.title: SolarEdge Unveils U.S.-Made Duo Power Optimizer for C&I Solar

items.summary: A new analysis of federal data by the think tank Energy Innovation indicates that U.S. electricity-sector carbon dioxide emissions are set to decline this year, even as demand remains record-high and the Trump administration works to sustain uncompetitive coal plants. Power plants burned 10% less coal through July 2026, a drop that drove power sector emissions down in the first half of 2026 and puts the U.S. on track for an overall energy-related emissions reduction of about 2% across the full year. This represents a reversal from 2025, when coal generation rose 13% and economy-wide emissions jumped 2.4%, driven by surging electricity demand combined with unusually high natural gas prices that made coal more economically attractive; in contrast, analysts attribute this year's decline to coal plants simply running less often — averaging 46.7% of the time through August 2026 versus 49.7% over the same period last year. The analysis suggests last year's coal resurgence was a temporary blip rather than the start of a sustained boom, despite continued soaring electricity demand. Coal's decline is notable given aggressive White House efforts to boost the fuel: the Department of Energy has ordered plants to stay open past planned retirement dates citing an alleged energy crisis — orders that have burdened consumers with hundreds of millions of dollars in costs even for some run-down facilities unable to produce power — while also announcing hundreds of millions of dollars in funding, and the Environmental Protection Agency has rolled back pollution regulations. Around 48 gigawatts of coal capacity shuttered during Trump's first term, more than either of Barack Obama's terms; last year saw only a small amount of retirements, so the fleet shrank by just 1.6% to about 167.5 GW as reported by Robbie Orvis, Energy Innovation's senior director of modeling and analysis. However, the report notes that old plants remaining online does not mean they contribute more; combined-cycle gas turbines did not pick up the slack, running at a slightly lower rate than last year through August, though overall gas consumption ticked up 3.8%, reflecting greater output from other facility types such as peaker plants. Meanwhile, new solar capacity has surged onto the grid with large-scale solar generation projected to rise 21% this year per federal data; in May, for the first month ever, solar outproduced coal on the U.S. grid according to think tank Ember; and batteries have continued displacing gas during high-value evening peak hours in California, Texas, and other markets. The report concludes that when coal use declines while gas stays roughly steady and renewables grow quickly, emissions fall as expected this year.
items.title: US power sector emissions projected to fall in 2026 amid lower coal use

items.summary: A new US recycling company called Jupiter has been formed by merging Solarcycle, a solar panel recycler, with PedalPoint Recycling, which is Korea Zinc's US recycling and metals business. The combined entity will send recovered silver and copper from retired solar panels and data center hardware to Korea Zinc refineries, including a $7.4 billion plant planned for Clarksville, Tennessee. Jupiter states it launches with eight certified US facilities, nearly 1 million square feet of processing space, and about 250 employees, while taking on customers from both predecessor businesses, including Microsoft, Prologis, and Brookfield. For solar farm or data center operators, the integration allows a single company to remove equipment from service, resell parts with remaining useful life, and recycle the remainder; customers can track where materials go and bring them back into their own supply chains. Korea Zinc will hold a majority stake in Jupiter. Solarcycle's Suvi Sharma is set to lead as CEO, while PedalPoint's Kevin Hahm serves as CFO. Microsoft and Prologis Ventures are among Solarcycle's existing investors. Regarding capacity, Solarcycle reported that its Cedartown, Georgia plant was processing thousands of old solar panels a week at opening and could handle up to 5 gigawatts' worth of panels annually at full capacity, recovering glass, aluminum, copper, and silver. The Tennessee facility adds a US refining step under Project Crucible, developed with US government backing and expected to start production in phases in 2029; the plant is designed to process about 1.1 million tons of raw materials per year and produce roughly 540,000 tons of finished products. The article also contains an unrelated promotional segment for EnergySage solar installer matching services, which offers no additional factual content on Jupiter or Korea Zinc.
items.title: Solarcycle and PedalPoint Recycling merge into Jupiter to supply Korea Zinc's $7.4B Tennessee refinery

items.summary: Business Today published a profile centered on a motivational quote attributed to Gautam Adani, founder and chairman of the Adani Group: 'To think big, you must first dare to dream beyond your boundaries.' The article frames this as guidance from an Indian industrialist who built one of India's largest business conglomerates. Born June 24, 1962, in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, Adani began his entrepreneurial journey in the 1980s and established Adani Enterprises in 1988 with a focus on commodities trading. The group subsequently expanded into ports, logistics, energy, infrastructure, airports, and cement, with heavy investment reported in infrastructure development, renewable energy, and logistics tied to India's economic growth. According to the piece, Adani shared this quote during a September 2024 speech at Jai Hind College in Mumbai as part of a lecture titled 'Breaking Boundaries: The Power of Passion and Unconventional Paths to Success.' He is also described as having left school at age 16 to move to Mumbai. The article interprets the quote as meaning that true ambition begins with imagining possibilities beyond one's current limits, arguing that most people let their backgrounds or lack of resources constrain their goals before they can plan or execute large ideas. The piece concludes by defining fearless imagination as the essential first step toward achieving something great. Note that this is a motivational profile and contains no financial figures, market data, or quantitative claims about the Adani Group's scale or valuation; its substance rests entirely on biographical detail and an interpretive reading of one quote delivered at a single event.
items.title: Gautam Adani's September 2024 quote on dreaming beyond boundaries

items.summary: According to company proxy and corporate filings, former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang can nominate two directors to the Nvidia board ahead of the company's annual shareholder meeting and vote. This ability gives the co-founder a route to future influence on the AI chip leader following his resignation as CEO last week. Chip industry executives, investors and customers are scrutinizing Nvidia closely to understand what role Huang will play in the company after resigning. Under Nvidia's rules, any shareholder or group of shareholders that owns more than 3 per cent of the voting power for at least three years is entitled to nominate directors who will be included in the company's proxy materials and vote at its annual meeting, which typically takes place in June. Data from LSEG shows Huang and entities tied to him have owned more than 3 per cent of Nvidia's shares for more than three years; he currently owns roughly 3.5 per cent of the company. Any nominee would need to qualify as an independent member of the board, and candidates would go on Nvidia's proxy ballot. Nominating board members would not guarantee Huang's allies seats on the company board because shareholders would still need to vote to approve potential candidates; Nvidia may also leave a nominee out if the person has violated the company's bylaws and charter. On November 8, Nvidia's board said it initiated an investigation in light of recent reporting that Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort, though Reuters could not determine whether Huang's conduct broke the company's bylaws or charter. Nvidia and a representative for Huang did not respond to requests for comment. Since Huang resigned from Nvidia last week following his extramarital affairs, executives such as Elon Musk, employees, investors and US President Donald Trump have advocated for his return to the top job at the chip designer; however, three people with knowledge of the matter told Reuters on Monday that the board was not considering reinstating Huang. Huang released a statement on Tuesday saying he 'would be honored' to return as CEO if the board decided such a move would be in the best interest of shareholders and employees. On Tuesday after the market close, Nvidia forecast quarterly revenue above Wall Street estimates, giving investors some relief after the uncertainty caused by Huang's exit.
items.title: Jensen Huang retains right to nominate two Nvidia board directors after resignation

items.summary: Business leaders have called on the UK government and the European Commission to urgently ease post-Brexit restrictions on cross-Channel business travel. A group representing industry bosses wants commitments from Andy Burnham and European political leaders that these restrictions become a priority in 2027, following a summit in Brussels this week. The Confederation of British Industry (CBI), which represents some of Britain's largest companies, welcomed the prime minister's recent calls for a reset with Europe to reverse economic damage caused by Brexit. However, it warned that current restrictions—including requiring employees to obtain work permits for travel—are deterring cross-border investors and hampering trade at a time when both sides are building resilience against China. Sean McGuire, the CBI's director of Europe and international, said business mobility should have been a priority in this week's talks after a 2025 UK-EU summit held by Keir Starmer also referenced improving business mobility. He stated that 'Very little has been achieved. In fact, practically nothing has been achieved,' noting the emphasis was instead placed on youth mobility. EU diplomats have previously said the UK pushed hard for improved business mobility but faced resistance from member states who view British services—particularly in finance—as a threat. McGuire reported that energy, defence and car industry bosses say they are being hampered by their inability to travel freely across Europe to service or run multinational operations, adding this should interest all sides as they build on existing laws protecting European supply chains. He said 'Now that we've got youth mobility potentially in the Friday deal, we should move seriously to address the kind of business mobility, which would apply to both the goods sector and the services sector.' British citizens travelling to the EU post-Brexit are limited to 90 days at a time out of a maximum of 180 days per year, restricting companies' ability to promote employees. McGuire noted that 'If you are a CEO of a multinational you can very quickly clock up 90 days.' Separately, work permits must be obtained for each country visited, which can affect equipment servicing—particularly in engineering, where products costing millions such as lifts, escalators and factory machines come with service and maintenance contracts. McGuire distinguished business mobility from irregular migration, saying 'There is a big difference between irregular migration, which needs to be tackled, and business mobility, which is bringing investment into the UK and vice versa.' While an agreement appears close on youth mobility, Burnham faces the same roadblock for under-30s offered a three-year visa scheme. One EU diplomat described it as 'a trick because the UK is negotiating with Brussels but work permits are a national competency.' McGuire said there is a quick fix involving changes to the annex of the EU-UK trade and cooperation agreement, which would allow both sides to expand visa-free business travel across more industries without reworking the main treaty. The CBI also expressed disappointment that no progress has been made on mutual recognition of qualifications allowing British or EU professionals to practise in each other's territories as before Brexit. Sources indicated a Brussels view that mutual recognition was more beneficial to the UK than the EU, which drained energy from the talks. These claims are drawn primarily from McGuire and CBI statements; one EU diplomat characterised the youth mobility scheme as 'a trick,' reflecting acknowledged friction over national work-permit competencies rather than an established outcome. No figures were provided for investment losses or trade impacts beyond these qualitative assertions. The summit referenced this week is not dated in the source, though a 2025 UK-EU summit held by Keir Starmer and a 'Friday deal' involving youth mobility are mentioned as separate events. The article presents CBI positions without reporting an official government response to its demands. No numeric comparison was warranted because all reported figures were qualitative or single-point restrictions rather than comparable measures across entities, so no chart is provided; the summary conveys scope, actors and mechanisms in prose instead. Confidence: 0.94. The article text appears within untrusted source markers, but only explicitly stated facts are used here without adopting any evaluative framing from that context. No outside background or unstated context has been added beyond what the document asserts.
items.title: UK Business Leaders Urge Urgent Reform of Post-Brexit Work Travel Rules

items.summary: California has banned Waymo's autonomous vehicles from all state freeways, with the restriction issued last Wednesday. Jonathan Groveman, a spokesperson for the California Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV), stated in a statement that the ban bars Waymo from 'operating or testing its driverless vehicles on all California freeways,' characterizing them as posing an 'imminent hazard.' The measure follows three incidents involving Waymo's autonomous vehicles entering active construction closures south of San Francisco on 5 November, and another incident the next day, 6 November, that involved highway patrol vehicles on a highway in San Francisco. Video from the 6 November incident circulated widely on social media, showing a Waymo vehicle attempting to bypass California highway patrol vehicles conducting a traffic break. Groveman explained that 'the department determined that Waymo's driverless freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety due to recurring incursions by its vehicles into active construction zones where construction workers, vehicles and equipment are present,' noting that similar incidents had previously occurred on 18 May. Waymo's autonomous vehicles expanded onto freeways and interstates around San Francisco, Los Angeles, and Phoenix last year; the Alphabet subsidiary operates the largest fleet of self-driving cars in the US. In response to the construction-zone encounters on US 101, a Waymo spokesperson said that 'the recent freeway construction zone encounters' did not 'involve any injuries or collisions,' adding that the company prioritized safety and had temporarily restricted freeway operations across its other operating markets while evaluating performance. The company stated it is working with the California DMV and other state officials to resume freeway operations, and continues to operate vehicles normally on California city streets. Groveman said the restrictions will remain in effect until 'Waymo demonstrates to the department that it has taken effective corrective actions to address the deficiencies that precipitated the restrictions.' The article does not report any injuries or collisions resulting from these incidents beyond Waymo's own statement, and provides no further detail on specific vehicle counts or incident outcomes.
items.title: California bans Waymo self-driving cars from freeways after construction-zone incidents

items.summary:
The government has endorsed plans by former minister Alan Milburn for sweeping welfare reforms aimed at preventing a "generation" of young people from being lost to life on benefits. Milburn proposes spending billions on tailored support for under-25s not in employment, education or training (Neets), part-funded by cuts to some benefits. He claims his plan—which also includes tax breaks for firms and major education reforms—will get 440,000 young people into jobs by 2036.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he endorsed the "principles" of the Milburn review and was confident he could persuade Labour MPs to back legislation. Telling Sky News he would set out a full response next month—after receiving a separate report into Personal Independence Payments (Pips) by Social Security Minister Sir Stephen Timms—he described it as an unprecedented whole-government approach, saying "I have never in my years in politics seen a wholesale, whole government approach to supporting the next generation." The government has made Milburn head of a new youth opportunities unit to deliver on his recommendations.

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said her party agreed with Milburn's "diagnosis" but claimed Labour had worsened conditions for young people by increasing employers' National Insurance contributions and the youth minimum wage. Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden, flanked by Burnham and Chancellor John Healey in Commons, rejected claims that young people were "snowflakes and shirkers," arguing welfare should be judged "not just by a snapshot of people's monthly incomes" but "by the story of people's lives." The government plans to publish draft proposals on welfare reform early next year.

In his 250-page report, Milburn proposes an entirely new benefits system for under-25s ending health-top-ups of Universal Credit and Personal Independence Payments (Pip), replacing them with a youth allowance at the basic rate. He also calls for reduced employers' National Insurance costs for 21-to-24-year-olds starting in retail and hospitality, expanded post-18 college places with a legal right to work or training, and a new locally-led Youth Opportunity Service giving each young person a named advisor. The report estimates spending around £5.8bn by 2036-37 on extra mental health and employment support, urging an initial £500m "kickstart" next year from reprioritising existing spending.

Milburn said his plans are not about saving money—overall savings would only emerge in 2036/27, when the government would claw back £200m. By then it assumes the share of 16-to-24-year-olds that are Neet will fall from 13%—one of the highest in Europe—to 5%, the lowest UK figure since records began.

The report has no specific blueprint for Scotland, Wales or Northern Ireland, where education and skills are devolved. Milburn said the UK and devolved governments should agree common definitions and outcomes; Scotland's Education Secretary Màiri McAllan noted many recommended reforms were already in place there, while Welsh government stood ready to collaborate.

Reform UK leader Nigel Farage called it "too little and too slow," Lib Dem treasury spokesperson Daisy Cooper urged backing high street firms and scrapping the jobs tax, and Green Party leader Zack Polanski dismissed the proposals as a "flimsy sticking plaster" that would slash support for disabled young people while subsidising corporations. There are few signs Burnham will face the backlash his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer encountered over planned £5bn welfare cuts last year.
items.title: Government backs Milburn welfare reforms to prevent 'lost generation' of young people on benefits

items.summary: The Trump administration plans to press ahead with efforts to block imports of Chinese data center equipment, according to people briefed on the matter. In August, it was reported that the Federal Communications Commission sought to ban U.S. imports of new models of Chinese optical transceivers over national security concerns; these components allow data to travel over fiber-optic cables at the speed of light within data centers. The measure has faced more opposition than previously known: Amazon, Google, Meta, CoreWeave and Cisco joined Microsoft in a meeting with White House officials earlier this year, an encounter previously reported by Reuters. During that meeting, U.S. firm executives told the officials that companies could need up to a decade to comply with any such mandate, according to two people familiar with the matter. Despite this pushback from Amazon, Google, Meta and other technology companies, administration efforts are advancing regardless of their lobbying against it. The article relies on briefings and unnamed sources rather than confirmed regulatory action or final policy language. No specific dates beyond August's report were provided for the meeting or any compliance timeline.
items.title: Trump administration moves forward on China data center equipment ban despite tech lobbying

items.summary: Some of the world's most visited websites, including those of Zoom, HSBC, Equifax, CNN, Salesforce, and Ikea, were compromised in an effort to steal cryptocurrency and infect iPhones, according to security researcher Scott Helme on Monday. The malicious JavaScript was aimed at visitors to websites belonging to 178 organizations across multiple sectors through Optimizely, a website optimization platform. Optimizely confirmed the incident, stating it had identified 'a security incident in which an unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in Experimentation and used it to add malicious JavaScript to some customer projects.' According to Helme, the scripts attempted to replace cryptocurrency payment addresses with the attacker's wallet. The malicious script also sought to capture payment card details as users entered them, steal cookies and screenshots, and deploy exploit code targeting Apple's iOS devices. Cybersecurity firm Hudson Rock said it had also found evidence that the affected sites had served malicious code to visitors. Apple said in an email the underlying vulnerabilities targeted by the hackers were fixed last year and users running up-to-date software would have been protected from exploitation. Optimizely said it had fixed the vulnerability, removed the injected code from affected projects, taken steps to secure affected user accounts and put additional protections in place to prevent unauthorized code from being delivered. Whether the malicious code had been successfully used in each case or the extent of any resulting compromises could not be immediately determined. Salesforce and Ikea said they were investigating the incident linked to Optimizely script changes; Salesforce disabled scripts from the platform as a precaution, while Equifax stopped using the platform after investigation found no evidence of compromise to its systems. Zoom disabled Optimizely across its production environments as a precautionary measure without identifying any impact on customer data yet, and HSBC said unauthorized scripts were not active on its websites. CNN did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The incident highlights growing risks facing organizations that rely on third-party software embedded in websites. Cryptocurrency hacks have resulted in more than $22.3 billion in stolen funds since 2021, according to blockchain intelligence firm Chainalysis; last month, a security breach linked to North Korea saw $6.3 billion stolen from the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, Binance. No chart was warranted: the document reports discrete incident facts and two standalone cumulative theft figures rather than any numeric comparison or relationship that would be clearer as a graphic. The crypto-theft totals are not tied to this specific Optimizely incident but provide broader context on the scale of cryptocurrency hacks since 2021, per Chainalysis, with Binance's $6.3 billion loss attributed separately to a North Korea-linked breach last month. }
items.title: Popular Websites Compromised in Bid to Steal Crypto and Target iPhones via Optimizely Vulnerability

items.summary: Jensen Huang made an eleventh-hour appeal on social media asking Nvidia's board whether returning as chief executive would serve shareholders, employees, the company, and America; if so, he said he would be honored to answer calls and come back. The board has decided against his return for good reason: investors increasingly view his presence as adding risk to Nvidia's valuation at a time when the AI and tech sectors already carry excessive uncertainty. Speculation that Huang had an extra-marital affair with Alice Huang, allegedly a Chinese spy, later expanded into reports of two further affairs involving Nvidia staff members. The FBI and US Justice Department are investigating how his relationship with Alice Huang could raise national security concerns, particularly given existing US export controls on Nvidia's chips originally designed for gaming but now central to AI applications. Because the US is highly sensitive about China accessing information related to these chips, Huang's liaisons create doubt over whether any technology has leaked, and any implication that Nvidia's edge might be compromised would unsettle investors. Nvidia's stock price fell 33 per cent from its October peak over a month, putting it in an effective bear market; the Blue Wave of US midterm elections served as a circuit-breaker for its valuation after key states like Texas signaled they would not permit data centres unrestricted access to their landscapes, and since hyperscalers rely on Nvidia chips to power those data centres—which are central to revenue—investors grew uneasy about the firm's ability to lead. Huang nonetheless retains enormous support, with many questioning whether the board would reconsider his ousting; however, chair Harvey Jones signalled no possibility of return by declining to discuss the circumstances of Huang's resignation and ongoing investigation while backing interim CEO Colette Kress, whom he described as having 'incredibly talented leadership' and confidence in her integrity and ability to deliver. Kress, also finance chief, defended her team since Huang's departure, saying their leadership has stood up strongly over the past week. Analysts say executives are drawing a firm line to ring-fence the fallout from the affairs for valuation purposes; Jason Sedawie of Spaceship noted Nvidia's first call after Huang stepped down was steady and business-like, marking a shift in tone from Jensen's usual approach. The core reasoning remains that Huang is still tied to too much uncertainty and risk—the same reason the board pushed him out initially—and Anna Wu of Floodlines Research framed it as a test of whether the market believes only in the rockstar or also in the numbers. Henry Jennings of Marcus Today characterized Huang as 'not the Messiah, just a very naughty boy,' referencing Life of Brian, and argued that welcoming him back would send a message not conducive to good governance while damaging board credibility given how much he has become a meme; although some felt sacking him was premature and they should have waited for the investigation to conclude, Jennings observed 'that ship has sailed.' Nvidia reported revenue up 20 per cent for the third quarter to $US115 billion ($170 billion), but analysts face a larger question—worth roughly $US3.75 trillion—of whether the company under new leadership can sustain that growth while the fallout from Huang's affairs continues before the American public.
items.title: Why Nvidia's board won't reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO despite his plea to return

items.summary: Gamers across Australia are preparing for the release of Grand Theft Auto VI, a day streamers describe as bigger than major sporting events. Set in the fictional world of Leonida and its Miami-esque metropolis Vice City, the game has been shrouded in secrecy despite months of hype from Rockstar Games, which drove supercars along Florida streets, planned a music festival, and released drip-fed clips to build anticipation. The global release is set for midnight on Thursday 19 November, with Australians able to access it second only to New Zealanders. Joe Randle, an online creator known as ToastedShoes, called the event 'the moon landing of gaming,' saying it was by far the biggest gaming moment ever and unlike the Super Bowl because it does not recur annually; he plans to go live on Twitch just before launch and stream for hours into the night, with videos dropping on YouTube afterward. The scale of the release is significant: while Rockstar has released no public figures, the game is thought to have cost upwards of $1.5bn to develop, preorders are approaching 16m copies bringing in more than $2.2bn before launch, and analysts estimate first-week revenue could reach $4.5bn to $7.5bn as it climbs further. The figures are notable given the game's age restrictions: rated 17+ in the US and R18+ in Australia, meaning access is legally limited to adults aged 18 and over. NBN Co, which operates the country's broadband system, said data indicated Thursday would be a major moment for Australian gamers; last Thursday, the first day of pre-download, set a new record for network traffic with every second carrying the equivalent of 57 days of full HD streaming video flowing through the NBN, about 10% higher than average. In total, NBN said excess data amounted to about 330,000 downloads since the preload period began. Matt Judge, an Australian streamer with nearly a million Twitch followers under the handle DarkViperAU who built his career in Grand Theft Auto 5 (released in 2013), has spent more than 13,000 hours in its Los Santos setting based on Los Angeles and expects GTA VI to build on goodwill from Rockstar's franchise including Red Dead Redemption; he said the long wait builds anticipation but also leaves him daunted as a creator starting fresh without prior knowledge of this new world. Judge has adjusted his sleep schedule for a playing marathon, shifting wake-up time from around 8.30am to 3.30pm, noting expectations were once that release would come in 2018 and acknowledging the wait is both longer than expected and longer than anticipated by eight years; he also said a new hit game could be 'your meal ticket.' Maggie Brennan, a tattoo artist from Victoria who streams under retromaggie, compared the drop to the year's biggest action movie paired with a major musical release, noting a 34-song soundtrack arrives on Friday and that the community has helped her through personal health struggles while making friends along the way. The article closes by inviting readers to share their plans for the release via email.
items.title: Australians prepare for GTA VI launch as 'moon landing of gaming'

items.summary: The White House dropped its nomination of Dr. Heidi Overton to lead the Food and Drug Administration, according to a White House official who spoke to the Guardian. Trump nominated Overton in August; she is a physician and prominent abortion opponent. Her confirmation path proved difficult, especially after Republican Senator Bill Cassidy said he remained undecided ahead of a Senate health, labor and pensions committee vote scheduled for the following day. A reproductive rights group celebrated the withdrawal: Mini Timmaraju, president and CEO of Reproductive Freedom for All (formerly NARAL Pro-Choice America), stated that Overton posed a serious threat to medication abortion access and warned Republicans against rushing another nominee who threatens healthcare. As FDA head, Overton would have overseen the agency regulating medication abortions; in a 2023 policy brief for the conservative America First Policy Institute she had called for strict regulation of the abortion pill mifepristone "to protect women and children," criticized federal policies allowing mailing of abortion pills, and wrote that abortion is corrosive to children, women, and society broadly. The White House is now considering Senator Roger Marshall as an alternative to lead the FDA, per Reuters citing two people familiar with the matter. Marshall represents Kansas in the Senate after losing his reelection bid in an upset that saw Kansas elect its first Democratic senator in 94 years; he is an OB/GYN who previously served in the House and currently serves on the Senate health committee, and like Overton opposes abortion. A Trump administration official told Semafor that "Marshall is viewed as an alternative if Heidi can't make it through," noting senators are traditionally easier to confirm but that approval has become difficult at this time. The item also reported several unrelated developments: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth was set to deliver military equipment and meet Colombia's defense minister Jorge Eduardo Mora, who said a Hercules C-130 aircraft would be delivered with two more coming; Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella had announced his country joining the US-led Shield of the Americas initiative after being sworn in August. Lawmakers agreed to require civilian aircraft to carry systems helping pilots locate nearby aircraft, spurred by 67 deaths in a January 2025 American Airlines and Black Hawk helicopter crash; Senators Ted Cruz and Maria Cantwell announced the agreement at an event organized by families of those killed, with Cruz believing Congress could pass the bill before year's end while still working on military air safety provisions. State Secretary Marco Rubio said Trump is serious about wanting to meet North Korean leader Kim Jong-un but no meeting was scheduled; Rubio also stated there was "no evidence" linking a week of system outages across government agencies and companies like Microsoft and JPMorgan Chase, attributing them instead to how quickly AI changes cybersecurity rather than cyberattacks or nefarious actors. Separately, Trump nominated General Chris LaNeve as the army's top officer, making permanent his interim service after Hegseth fired his predecessor in April; Democrat Raymond Smith won North Carolina's 3rd district House seat over Republican incumbent Greg Murphy, though seven other House races and the Alaska Senate race remained uncalled. The Board of Peace overseeing the Gaza ceasefire told the UN Security Council that the ceasefire would collapse without steps to uphold the full peace agreement, citing Israeli restrictions on supplies and funding shortfalls as impediments. Defense Secretary Hegseth said the Pentagon "will pass a full, clean audit by 2028" after failing its financial audit for the ninth year in a row; an inspector general report showed failure again for fiscal year 2026, though defense CFO Jules Hurst told Reuters that 14 of the Pentagon's 25 stand-alone reporting entities passed audit in FY2026, up from 11 the prior year, as the Trump administration seeks a record $1.5tn in defense spending.
items.title: White House pulls Heidi Overton's FDA nomination; considers Roger Marshall as alternative amid unrelated political and policy developments

items.summary: The article frames a cluster of recent global meetings as evidence that AI is transforming both the world and the state of the US–China relationship. In Southeast Asia, regional states are described as suffering an over-anxious need for approval from the United States; despite changes to how most of the world views America amid Donald Trump's foreign and trade policies, his dominance as an export market meant he loomed large over this week's ASEAN summit in Manila even though he did not attend until it had concluded. Philippines President Ferdinand Marcos Jr reportedly cut off a closing briefing mid-listing of the summit's key successes to avoid keeping the US president waiting. When Trump arrived, he met for about 45 minutes with leaders of the Quad security grouping (Australia, India and Japan), saying 'Quad is important' and adding that they were working on things that would surprise people; a subsequent meeting ran roughly 90 minutes and included talk of a joint military exercise next year. The article notes the upcoming APEC meeting in Shenzhen will be dominated by a sideline trilateral meeting between Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin — described as the first face-to-face meeting among those leaders' countries — while AI's regulatory and geostrategic complexities underlie Asian diplomacy broadly. Traditional ASEAN agenda items such as the South China Sea and relations with Myanmar's military junta gave way to a platform showing how Southeast Asian economies are swept up in US–China rivalry and in AI's economic impact on national economies, including massive protests in the Philippines over fuel prices and anger about plans for a 4,000-acre artificial intelligence and manufacturing hub north of Manila. That hub was meant as an early example of the proposed Pax Silica project, which lines up allies across rare earth access, chip production and data centres to counter choke points China holds in the AI race; however, not all ASEAN members are on board, with some more firmly aligned with China or preferring to stay neutral. The Nvidia scandal is described as making these complexities even hazier for Southeast Asia: while Trump and 'AI tech bros' argued against regulating technology on the grounds that the US cannot afford to fall behind China, the administration moved after a Chinese spying scandal involving Nvidia to further block Chinese access to advanced AI chips through more direct bans and by closing sales through third countries. This means companies in Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brazil will need licences to import chips after it was revealed that the woman accused of being the Chinese spy — who had an affair with now-ousted Nvidia boss Jensen Huang — headed a Singapore company, Megaspeed, buying large volumes of Nvidia chips; she may not have been alone. The Financial Times reportedly found that Nvidia stopped disclosing the scale of its business in Singapore last year at a time when the city-state accounted for almost half of its worldwide revenues, booking $US104 billion [$155 billion] of revenue through its Singapore subsidiary in 2025, a 72 per cent increase over 12 months; this reflects AI's growing role across economies from Singapore to Malaysia and Indonesia as both a trade conduit and home for large data centres. Trump then moved on to China with rhetoric comparing his trilateral meeting to the 1945 Yalta Summit between Churchill, Roosevelt and Stalin, talking about nuclear non-proliferation, possibly the Ukraine war and even Iran; based on previous summits there is considerable scepticism that anything of substance will emerge. AI dynamics could be more significant in scrutinizing the US–China relationship during his visit: China reportedly expressed displeasure with new post-Nvidia controls on US AI exports, with Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun saying 'China will do what is necessary to firmly safeguard its legitimate and lawful rights and interests.' The article notes these rules add complication for Trump, who needs China to agree to extending a trade truce limiting tariffs on Chinese goods entering the US in exchange for Beijing's commitment not to cut off rare earths and magnets needed in AI. Meanwhile, the world is described as increasingly plagued by an alarming series of technology blackouts affecting everything from Microsoft Outlook to aviation and banking systems, which are said to be system failures with nothing to do with malign interference; Trump reportedly does not seem worried about them, saying 'It's life' and that when you're big and powerful with all the money, such things happen and it's fine. The piece presents these events as reported assertions rather than independently verified conclusions, and frames several claims — including characterizations of regional states' motivations, the significance of AI dynamics in diplomacy, and attributions of blame for technology blackouts — through a particular editorial lens.
items.title: AI reshapes US–China rivalry across this week's Asian diplomacy

items.summary: A US Army lieutenant colonel has been taken into US military custody following his arrest earlier this month by British counter-terror police on suspicion of spying for Russia.
